text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- A study by consulting firm Brog Servives shows that in the week after they were freed, retail prices of fuel at petrol stations rose on average by 4.9 percent and diesel increased the most -- by seven percent.

- The European Commission is threatening Poland with international arbitration over its protection for production of vehicles such as trucks. It says measures introduced by Poland in mid-1994 including keeping duties on such vehicles or lowering the age-limit for those imported from the EU, infringe Poland's association agreement with the Union.
- Warsaw city's treasury will get 30 million to 35 million zlotys for six hotels sold to Austrian company Bau Holding. The ground on which the hotels stand is alone worth that sum.

- The Zielonogorsk branch of gas company Polski Gornictwo Gazowy signed a a credit agreement with a consortium set up by Bank Handlowy and PKO SA to finance development of local gas and crude oil deposits. Both banks will lend $87.5 million.
- Amerbank will today change its bourse listing from the parallel to the main market. The bank is also preparing for a further share issue. A public offer will be made in the first half of this year.
- The management of the CTO over-the-counter market will probably today examine insurer Polisa's request to remove its series G and K shares from the registry of shares traded off-bourse.
- National Investment Fund Progress is preparing for its bourse debut, planned for the second quarter of this year.
- Bank Handlowy, as a member of CeTO, has submitted a motion to have Ostrow Wielkopolski's bonds entered onto the register of the over-the-counter market's securities.
